text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Warmbad community in southern Namibia wants to claim back the settlement's hot springs, currently owned by a South African, to launch a community-based tourism project.

- President Sam Nujoma has again attacked gays and lesbians, this time at the opening of the ruling Swapo Youth League congress, and warned them to refrain from imposing homosexuality on wider society.
- The Youth League has said President Nujoma should be allowed to stand for a third term.
- Six months after the launch of Namibian Press & Tools, a subsidiary of German Company Weser-Metall-Uniformtechnik, the company plans to extend its operations, a company official said.
- The National Theatre of Naimbia faces closure due to a shortage of funds.
- The viability of an ostrich abatoir is being questioned after its launch in Keetmanshoop last Friday. The abatoir is due for completion within two years.
- An agreement for increased control measures at border posts between Namibia and Zambia is to be signed by the two governments soon, to crack down on smuggling and illegal border crossings.
